subject: Meteorology
title: Convective Initiation
description: A micro-lesson that makes Convective Initiation usable.

hook.text: Knowing where the first storms will pop up—convective initiation—is one of forecasting's toughest challenges.

buildup.text: The atmosphere might be primed for storms everywhere, but they only fire along specific boundaries or features.

discovery.text: Old outflow boundaries, drylines, and terrain features act as triggers—subtle lines visible only on fine-scale data.

twist.text: Satellite imagery can spot cumulus fields starting to bubble up—the first visual hints of initiation.

climax.text: Predicting initiation to within 50 km and one hour remains a frontier—even the best models miss the mark regularly.

punchline.text: We know storms are coming—but exactly where and when is still a guess.

quiz.question: Why is convective initiation difficult to forecast?
options: It depends on subtle, small-scale boundary features
